correctness.rationale: For fixed pairs of diagonal values (d_v,s_v), an arrow gives one linear constraint on its two independent radical coordinates: q solutions if its endpoint labels differ, q² otherwise. Parallel and antiparallel arrows still use separate variables. Expansion over individually labeled edges forces the (d_v,s_v) labels constant on each spanning component, including isolates, giving the claimed q^|E| prefactor and sum. The algebra has q^(|V|+|E|) elements; dividing by its square and substituting X−1=q²/(q−1), Y−1=q−1 in the rank-subset definition gives exactly the stated Tutte evaluation. The edgeless case gives probability one, and two vertices with r parallel arrows give q^−2+(q²−1)q^(−r−2). Independently enumerated ordered products via basis multiplication, not the frozen commutator shortcut: 7936 for the two opposite arrows over F4 (using x²+x+1), and 4480 for each of two orientations of a three-edge multigraph with an isolated vertex over F2. The frozen verifier does check seven prime-field cases against the sum, but it evaluates the commutator coordinate formula rather than independently implementing xy and yx; this and the case-count description are documentation limitations, not proof defects. The Potts partition function equals the count divided by q^|E|, not the unscaled count.

The earlier rank formula is m−|Z|+r_G(S), with multiplicity q^(m−|Z|)(q−1)^|S| for each d,S. Its proof eliminates each nonmonochromatic arrow separately and identifies the remaining rank with that of an incidence matrix. Parallel rows are proportional (including when the orientations are opposite); they do not alter the component-rank identity.
The earlier multigraph conjugacy theorem treats the different invariant of conjugation by units and has different evaluation points.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The additive centralizer size from the prior rank is q^(|Z|+k(S)). Multiplying by the multiplicity above gives q^m(q−1)^|S|q^k(S) for each d,S. For each S there are q^k(S) allowed choices of d. This gives the exact multigraph count with the same argument and no new ingredient, even though the earlier rank theorem states only the simple case.
